objective: Retain the two most recent complete recoverable backup snapshots on 112 and substantially reduce historical logs.

backupPolicy.sortBy: snapshot manifest createdAt, independent of whether the associated deployment succeeded
preserve: the selected complete snapshot payloads and manifests
active or otherwise referenced recovery operations
small historical manifests, activation and validation evidence
current production data and the complete migrated project originals
cleanupCandidates: unreferenced historical release copies after retaining the live release and releases required by the two recovery points

logPolicy.semantics: Age and size are upper bounds; capacity may evict logs before seven days. This is not a seven-day minimum retention guarantee.
logPolicy.applyConfiguration: reload the existing journald service only when its supported CanReload contract has been verified

alternatives: Continue retaining all historical data; inspection showed approximately 140.4 GB of backup and recovery materials.
Delete every backup; this would remove the requested recovery coverage.
Retain the latest two complete recoverable points and their required release material, remove obsolete data under publication locks, and cap journal retention.
reason: The user explicitly chose two recent backups and authorized substantial log cleanup. Retaining complete recovery points and necessary release dependencies preserves the requested recovery scope while releasing large obsolete copies.
executionConditions: verify the selected recovery points with their pinned manifests
hold the existing publication lock exclusively during destructive backup operations
refuse active references, unexpected symlinks, mounts or changed target identities
record actual freed space and production health after execution
rollbackBoundary: Deletion of old backup data and old logs is intentional and irreversible; the retained recovery points are preserved. New retention configuration may be reverted without restoring deleted historical data.
